notes: Arcade flight-model reference values. Source quality tags: [A] official fact sheet / flight-manual-derived, [B] Jane's- or book-cited encyclopedia infobox, [C] secondary spec aggregator, [D] forum or game wiki (pilot or manual quotes, unverified). km/h conversions: 1 kt = 1.852 km/h, 1 ft/min = 0.00508 m/s.

vmax_sl_kmh.note: 381 kt at sea level, clean (Wikipedia infobox citing Jenkins 1998 p.54 [B]; MILAVIA 706 km/h [C]). USAF fact sheet gives 420 mph (676 km/h) without altitude or configuration [A]. Picked 706 because it is the explicit sea-level clean figure.

vstall_kmh.note: 120 kt at 30,000 lb (Wikipedia infobox citing a 2001 SimHQ article [D-quality citation]). Configuration not stated; treat as approximate.

g_limit.note: +7.33/-3.0 g symmetric at about 30,000 lb; +5.8 asymmetric; drops to +5.0/-2.0 near max gross weight [C/D, flight-manual-derived]. Wikipedia infobox lists no g limit.

vmax_sl_kmh.note: Sources disagree: ru-Wikipedia 950 km/h with normal combat load (Su-25K) [B]; en-Wikipedia 975 km/h at sea level for late-production Su-25/Su-25K (Jane's 2003-04) [B]; MILAVIA 850 km/h for Frogfoot-A (Gordon & Dawes 2004) [C]. Picked 950: the loaded figure from a 1980s-production variant, between the clean and conservative values.

vstall_kmh.note: Landing speed, not stall (ru-Wikipedia, 210 km/h [B]). A DCS test thread gives landing-configuration stall of 220 km/h light to 260-270 km/h fully loaded for the Su-25T [D]. No published clean stall figure found.

g_limit.note: +6.5 g with normal combat load; +5.2 g with maximum load (all three sources agree) [B].

vmax_sl_kmh.note: Mach 1.2 / 800 kt at sea level (Wikipedia infobox for F-16C Block 50/52, citing Frawley, International Directory of Military Aircraft [B]). No Block 30-specific figure found; Block 30 (F110-GE-100) is comparable. High-altitude figure is Mach 2.05.

vstall_kmh.note: Approach speed, not stall. SKYbrary Vapp 150 kt [C, page blocked to fetch; value seen in search extract]. A line pilot on f-16.net reports 160-175 kt at 11 deg AOA [D]. f-16.net pilots state there is no single published stall speed. Picked 150 kt as the lightweight approach figure.

g_limit.note: +9 g (Wikipedia infobox [B]; widely published design limit).

climb_m_s.note: 50,000 ft/min, from secondary aggregators [C]; Wikipedia infobox omits climb. An early F-16 pilot on f-16.net describes 20,000 ft/min easy in AB and 5,000-7,000 ft/min loaded [D], so 254 m/s is a clean peak, not typical.

vmax_sl_kmh.note: Mach 1.2 / 800 kt at sea level (Wikipedia infobox, F-15C, citing USAF fact sheet, Jane's and TO 1F-15A-1 [A/B]). High-altitude figure is Mach 2.5.

vstall_kmh.note: 123 kt level flight, power off, speed brake in, gear and flaps down, 39,000 lb (forum post quoting flight-manual data [D]). Landing-configuration stall, not clean. Approach speed is about 150 kt (same search extract).

g_limit.note: Sources disagree: Wikipedia +9 [B]; flight-manual limit without the Overload Warning System is +7.33 [D, forum]. Picked 9 as the infobox figure for an OWS-equipped F-15C; use 7.33 if modeling non-OWS jets.

climb_m_s.note: 67,050 ft/min, maximum with 3 pylons (Wikipedia infobox [B]). Peak figure, likely not at the sea-level start of the climb.

vmax_sl_kmh.note: 1,500 km/h near the ground (airforce-technology [C]; Russian-language summary [C]). War Thunder wiki lists 1,400 km/h at sea level [D, game]. Picked 1,500 as the more widely quoted figure. Wikipedia infobox gives only the high-altitude Mach 2.3+ (2,450 km/h).

vstall_kmh.note: Touchdown/landing speed, not stall. Forum post quoting the pilot's manual gives touchdown 250-260 km/h at typical weight, flare 280-290 km/h [D]; War Thunder wiki landing speed 260 km/h [D]. No published stall speed found.

g_limit.note: +9 g (Wikipedia infobox citing RAC MiG [B]; airforce-technology [C]).

climb_m_s.note: 330 m/s (Wikipedia infobox citing Flug Revue [B]; airforce-technology [C]). Peak figure, light weight.

vmax_sl_kmh.note: Sources disagree: en-Wikipedia 1,315 km/h (M1.06) at sea level for Su-24MK (Sukhoi, Combat Aircraft since 1945, deagel [B/C]); ru-Wikipedia 1,400 km/h at 200 m without stores for Su-24M [B]. Picked 1,315 as the conservative figure closer to a loaded strike jet.

vstall_kmh.note: Landing speed, not stall: 285-310 km/h (ru-Wikipedia, Su-24M [B]). Picked the low end. No stall figure found.

g_limit.note: Sources disagree: en-Wikipedia +6 (operational) [B]; ru-Wikipedia +6.5 max operational [B]. Picked 6 as the conservative operational limit.

climb_m_s.note: 150 m/s (30,000 ft/min), en-Wikipedia Su-24MK infobox citing aggregated sources [C]. Single source; treat as approximate.
